title: verify: run a flow locally and report the node trace, before it is submitted
body:
epic:#34659#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnXJdSZifpEN5i7aU

Filing gate: ④ a child of the cross-lane parent #34659 (the 「MCP 二期与问数」 epic), filed on the maintainer's word in this seat's chat, 2026-11-17, verbatim: 「三点都同意，按最终计划把后续里程碑的卡全部立出来」, and, on the list of thirteen cards the seat then showed: 「同意」. The ruling records are #34659 comment 6940528935 and #34691 comment 6943107981. Readings: objectstack `a0326b06`, cloud `53a5844`, 2026-11-17.

## Why

A flow is the item most often saved clean and dead at run time, and the one a static check sees least of. Nothing lets an author trigger it once against a local runtime and read what each node did.

Who acts: the server lane (`packages/verify`, `packages/cli`, `packages/services/service-automation`). Reader: an author, or an AI client, before submitting a flow.

## Evidence

- `os verify` boots the stack and proves CRUD, row-level security, reference shapes, delete behaviour, unique scope and dashboard windows (`packages/cli/src/commands/verify.ts`); none of its proofs runs a flow.
- The hosted product has a flow test tool and withholds it from the MCP door.

## Scope

- A local flow run: given a flow and a triggering record or input, run it against the booted stack and print each node's status, the first failure with its code, and what the run wrote.
- A flow that would write runs against the ephemeral stack only.
- Only this piece of the local export, simulate and submit loop is built now (E3 = phased).

## Done when

- A flow whose node type has no executor, and one whose trigger never binds, are both reported by the local run with the node named.

## Relations

- Parent: #34659. Ruling: E3 = phased.
- Dedup, open and closed: none found for `flow local test run`.
